ASSEMBLY
1 Front module slides UP into the dome's side grooves from below. Nothing retains it at this point.
2 It seats against the lip; 4.5 mm of its edge is captured all round, with 0.5 sliding clearance.
3 Bottom plate goes on. Its top face is the module's datum - the module's bottom edge lands on it and can no longer drop.
4 Six M3 screws pull the bottom plate up into the dome bosses. No fastener touches the facade.
NOTES
a ONE FRONT PIECE, YES - but the diffuser stays separate. You cannot print an even diffuser; the printed part is the frame and
the cavity, and the Glowforge-cut opal acrylic drops into a pocket from behind. Everything that must stay in register with
everything else - matrix aperture, grilles, mic ports, diffuser - is now on ONE part, so there are no stacked tolerances.
b The facade went 3 -> 4 mm. Two 50x45 sealed boxes on an unsupported 3 mm plate will flex and buzz; it is a baffle now, not a cover.
Ribs run from each baffle ring out to the perimeter for the same reason.
c AIR GAP IS A GUESS. 12 mm is ~0.7x the 16.7 mm LED pitch, the usual starting point for not seeing 48 dots through opal.
Test-print the crescent corner before committing - this is the one number most likely to need changing.
d FIXINGS ARE WALL LUGS, NOT FLOOR BOSSES. Each lug is a pad that projects inward off the dome wall with a blind heat-set hole; the
screw comes up through the bottom plate and grabs it. Lugs live at the perimeter where the plate needs support anyway, and they
cost no floor area - which matters, because the floor is fully spoken for. Clearances per lug are in the key beside the plan.
e NO LUG ON THE FRONT EDGE. The speaker bodies own both front corners and the tray owns the middle, so there is nowhere to put one.
It does not need one: the plate's front edge is captured between the seating ledge and the front module's bottom edge.
f TPA2016 moved to the REAR WALL at y=40. There is no floor left for it, and the speaker leads are shortest from there.
Bridge-tied outputs: do NOT common the two speakers' negatives (HARDWARE.md).
